Hi Laura, Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As discussed, we want to pull together a short feasibility checklist so your teams can see what Redwood would need from a contract and operational perspective for a combined pilot (Oakridge K12 — FERPA; CommunityBankOne — GLBA).

Attached: Oakridge_DPA_questions.pdf (initial questionnaire), Redwood_subprocessors_list_20270321.csv, MAP_v1.0.xlsx (mutual action plan template)

High-level asks from Redwood to start assessment:
- Confirm data types we’ll see in requests (PII, student records, financial account numbers).
- Residency requirements (EU/US-only, state residency for K12?).
- BAA/FERPA requirements: is Oakridge requesting a HIPAA BAA in addition to FERPA controls, or only FERPA addendum?
- GLBA-specific requirements from CommunityBankOne: dedicated capacity? encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
- Any required third-party attestations (SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001) beyond our standard docs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura & Samir to return the filled questionnaire by Thu 25 Mar
2) Redwood to return a short feasibility memo and a redline-ready addenda skeleton by Mon 29 Mar
3) Legal review meeting (30 min) week of 29 Mar to walk through any high-risk asks

CC’ing Grace (Legal) and Vivek (Solutions) to keep the right folks in the loop.

Thanks —
Aisha

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear list. A few clarifications from the Oakridge side:
- This is a K–12 district (student PII + education records). FERPA addendum is required; we typically do not sign HIPAA BAAs for student records unless there's a covered health program. So for Oakridge, FERPA-centric controls are the priority.
- Residency: district policy requires US-only storage and processing for student records. We are not asking for EU residency.
- Subprocessors: please provide a current list (CSV is perfect) and an assurance on the frequency of updates and notification method.
- Data flow question: do you persist embeddings or other derived representations, and can those be scoped per-tenant (i.e., we want embeddings turned off unless explicitly permitted)?

We’ll fill in the questionnaire and flag any items outside our standard procurement flow.

One more ask: if Redwood can provide an explicit statement on ability to support FERPA disclosure redactions (e.g., ability to exclude names from logs and audit exports) that would help accelerate our security team review.

Best,
Laura

Laura — thank you, this is helpful. Quick responses inline:

- Residency: we can commit to US-only processing for the pilot and document the region constraint in the addendum.
- Subprocessors: the attached CSV is our current list; we notify customers via the Console and email for material changes. We update the list quarterly and can provide an audit log of updates on request.
- Embeddings/persistence: by default our hosted API persists minimal model caches for performance; we can provide a tenant-scoped toggle to disable embeddings and prefix/KV caching for Oakridge in the pilot. This would be implemented as a config flag on the route.
- Logs & redaction: we already support token-level scrubbing via configurable pipelines and can exclude name fields from audit exports. We will include a write-up in the feasibility memo explaining where and how data is stored and the retention windows.

Next: I’ll ask Grace to prepare a short redline-ready FERPA addendum skeleton and list of open negotiation items. Vivek — can you confirm whether the pilot for CommunityBankOne requires Dedicated (reserved GPU) or if burst capacity is sufficient?

Attaching MAP_v1.0.xlsx for a proposed timeline and owners.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Vertical addenda feasibility: K12 + community bank pilot — scope & ops checklist

Aisha / Vivek —

I reviewed the questionnaire and Aisha's notes. A few legal items we should flag upfront for both addenda (FERPA + GLBA):

1) Data classification: need explicit language that student education records and account-holder financial data are treated as regulated data categories with stronger confidentiality and limited retention.
2) Subprocessor notices: our standard window is 30 days for material changes; Oakridge asked for notification method — email + Console notification is fine but they may request a contractual 30-day notice for specified processors.
3) Embeddings / derived representations: include a clause that Redwood will not use customer-derived embeddings for model training and will allow per-tenant disabling. Need operational confirmation from infra regarding cache persistence and retention windows (exact TTLs).
4) Audit & access logs: provide a sample schema for audit logs and confirm retention and export capabilities. They may request SFTP or Drive export for audits.
5) KMS requirement: for CommunityBankOne, if they require customer-managed keys we need to confirm support for HSM-backed keys and whether that applies to Dedicated only.
6) SLA exceptions / penalties: bank may request latency/availability SLAs for Dedicated pool. We should assess the margin impact before committing.

I'll draft a FERPA addendum skeleton and a parallel GLBA addendum with callouts for KMS/SLA sections. Aisha — please collect the answers to caching TTLs and whether embeddings can be fully disabled at route-level vs. service-level.

Grace

Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference
